newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico same-day Cetes rate ends down on liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Mexico same-day Cetes rate ends down on liquidity.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed 140 basis points lower at a session low 21.50 percent on Wednesday due to lack of paper on offer and greater liquidity in the system, traders said.

"There have been dealers stepping in to buy term instruments since yesterday, and taking paper out of the system. Furthermore, some today were taking advantage of good positions and demand to keep paper scarce," a trader said.
Traders said that greater demand for paper was due to the need to cover positions ahead of the annual money market convention taking place this weekend.
"Dealers are looking to cover positions for four to five days so trading can be light over the coming days. They already want to head off," another trader said.
Traders also said that a strong peso gave room for manoeuvre to cut secondary rates.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed 60 basis points down at 24 percent.

Liquidity shortages had been estimated at 8.47 billion pesos, but were offset by greater than expected government spending of 2.5 billion pesos and money returning to the system after the long weekend.
Banco de Mexico earlier further offset liquidity shortages by injecting 3.906 billion pesos through three credit auctions, which it assigned between 24.11 percent and 24.93 percent.
Liquidity shortages on Thursday will arise from credit maturities totalling 1.800 billion pesos.
